title: Species differ from varieties only in their intermediates having existed formerly

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Species differ from varieties only in their intermediates having existed formerly

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The only distinction between species and well-marked varieties is that varieties are known or believed to be connected by intermediate gradations at present, whereas species were connected by them in the past; species should therefore be treated, like genera, as combinations made for convenience.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Hereafter we shall be compelled to acknowledge that the only distinction between species and well-marked varieties is, that the latter are known, or believed, to be connected at the present day by intermediate gradations, whereas species were formerly thus connected.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIV, “Recapitulation and Conclusion”; section “Effects of its adoption on the study of Natural history”. Scope: species and varieties of all organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch14-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.59

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Continuity and divergence can be quantified for many groups. The exclusive, conceptual claim about the only distinction and classificatory convenience is not fully empirically resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure genetic and phenotypic continuity within named varieties and species, including fossil or phylogenetic evidence for lost intermediates, and test whether discontinuity alone distinguishes the categories. Continuity gradients would support the empirical portion, but cannot establish that the distinction is only one of convenience.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Reproductive isolation provides distinctions beyond observed intermediates.

Species and variety are partly conventional categories with multiple concepts.

Former intermediates are absent by definition and often unpreserved.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.65
data adequacy: 0.62
data existence: 0.85
discriminating power: 0.38

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The proposed distinction can be compared with other species criteria only where ranks, geography and genetic data coincide, which is a subset of organisms. Because rank assignments already encode the presence of intermediates, a checklist test is weakly discriminating. The result can show how present ranks behave and cannot establish that former connection is the only difference.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare named varieties and named species for the presence of living morphological or genetic intermediates, and for other candidate distinctions such as reproductive isolation and genetic-cluster gaps. The claim is confirmed if the presence or absence of living intermediates is the only consistent separator, and refuted if species and varieties also separate cleanly by isolation or genetic distance once intermediates are held constant.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Reproductive isolation and genetic clusters are not fields in these taxonomic databases and would have to be joined from separate studies.

Fossil intermediates that would show species were formerly connected are unavailable for the great majority of living species pairs.

Taxonomists already use living intermediates to decide variety versus species, so the contrast is partly the definition under test.
